issues.sym: The brake pedal may suddenly bend or give way under your foot, leaving you with little or no braking.
issues.why: The brake pedal arm on some cars was not strong enough. Recall 24V752 has dealers add a reinforcement to the pedal arm.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls right away. If the recall is open, have it done before driving much, and get the car towed if the pedal ever feels loose or sinks.

issues.t: Loose battery or high-voltage cable can cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly a burning smell, warning messages or a car that will not start, but a fire can start with no warning, even while parked.
issues.why: The 12-volt battery positive cable or a high-voltage connector on the plug-in hybrid may not have been tightened at the factory, so the joint overheats. Recall 23V623 covers it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Until the recall is done, park outside and away from buildings. Have the dealer inspect and tighten the connections for free.

issues.t: Pedestrian warning sound may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: You may not hear the low-speed warning sound the car should make when backing up in electric mode.
issues.why: The external pedestrian alert speaker on some plug-in hybrids was missing or not plugged in. Recall 23V696 covers it.
issues.next: Be extra careful backing up around people, and have the dealer install or connect the speaker for free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: The center screen stays blank or shows 'camera system unavailable' when you shift into reverse. Some owners also report the whole screen freezing.
issues.why: A software or display fault can stop the camera picture from showing. Recall 25V246 covers it, and some owners have waited for parts.
issues.next: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder when reversing. Check your VIN for the recall and ask the dealer to update or repair the display.

issues.t: Rear seat belts can twist and not retract (recall)
issues.sym: A rear outer seat belt twists, gets stuck pulled out, or won't wind back in, which can make it hard to secure a child seat or booster.
issues.why: The rear outboard belt retractors on some cars do not reel the belt in properly, so it may not hold a passenger as designed. Recall 26V510 covers it.
issues.next: Do not seat a passenger behind a belt that will not retract. Check your VIN for the recall and have the belt repaired for free.

issues.t: Tire label shows wrong load capacity (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The tire and loading sticker in the driver door jamb lists the wrong maximum load.
issues.why: The placard printed an incorrect vehicle capacity weight, which could lead an owner to overload the car. Recall 24V175 replaces the label.
issues.next: Do not load the car based on the old sticker. Have the dealer install the corrected label for free.

issues.t: Tire and rim size missing from label (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The certification label is missing the tire and rim size information.
issues.why: Some labels were printed without the required tire and wheel details. Recall 24V209 replaces the label.
issues.next: Have the dealer replace the label for free; it matters when buying replacement tires.

issues.t: Driver-assist systems shut off with sensor warnings
issues.sym: Adaptive cruise control and forward collision warning turn off with 'sensor blocked' or 'service required' messages, often in rain, snow, fog or strong sun.
issues.why: The front radar and camera lose their view in bad weather or when dirty, and some owners report faults even in clear conditions that dealers struggle to fix.
issues.next: Clean the front radar area and windshield in front of the camera. If the warnings appear in good weather, have the dealer check sensor alignment and software.

issues.t: Unexpected hard braking or steering from driver-assist
issues.sym: The car brakes hard with nothing ahead, or lane keeping pulls the wheel in a way you did not expect.
issues.why: The forward collision and lane assist systems can misread the road or traffic and react when there is no real danger.
issues.next: Report it to the dealer and to NHTSA, and ask for a sensor check and any software update. You can turn lane keeping off in the settings until it is resolved.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power or stalling
issues.sym: The car stops accelerating, shuts off in traffic or won't restart, and steering and brakes can get heavy when it happens. Warning lights often come on.
issues.why: Owners have reported a mix of causes, including electrical and engine control faults, and some cars made repeated dealer visits without a clear fix.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get off the road safely and have the codes read. Keep a record of each event and dealer visit, as repeated repairs can matter under lemon laws.

issues.sym: The car won't start or loses power to many systems at once; heated mirrors or the rear defroster may stop working with a low battery warning.
issues.why: The 12-volt battery runs down or loses charge, and the car shuts off features to save power.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. If it keeps happening, ask the dealer to check for software updates and any power drain.

issues.t: Driver door won't latch, mostly in cold weather
issues.sym: The door won't latch or lock, or it can open after it seemed closed, especially when it is cold.
issues.why: The door latch mechanism can stick or fail to catch, which several owners report in freezing weather.
issues.next: Do not drive with a door that will not latch. Have the latch inspected and replaced under warranty.

issues.t: Center screen or gauge display freezes or goes black
issues.sym: The touchscreen freezes, goes black or drops Apple CarPlay; the instrument display can also go dark. The backup camera and some alerts may be lost at the same time.
issues.why: Software and display hardware faults in the infotainment and cluster screens.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Try restarting the car. If it keeps happening, have the dealer install updates or replace the display under warranty, and check whether the camera recall applies.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid loses drive power at highway speed
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses power and slows down on the highway, may refuse to shift out of Park once stopped, and can die again soon after a restart. There may be no warning light.
issues.why: An owner report points to a fault in the electric side of the hybrid powertrain; the exact cause was not confirmed. Separate owner complaints to NHTSA also describe sudden loss of drive power.
issues.next: Get to the shoulder safely and call for a tow rather than repeatedly restarting. Have the dealer read the hybrid system codes and check for software updates.

issues.t: Check engine light with throttle body error
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a chime and a 'throttle body' error message, sometimes with other warnings, then may go away on its own.
issues.why: A communication or sensor fault involving the electronic throttle body sets a network trouble code (such as U1202). The root cause was not identified in the owner report.
issues.next: Have the codes read while the light is on and ask the dealer to check for software updates and wiring faults at the throttle body. The car is under warranty, so keep records of each visit.
